title.narrative: NORCAP Middle-East Crisis Respons Humanitarian Surge

description.narrative: Humanitarian secondments in Syria, Lebanon, Palestine Through the provision of expert to partners responding to crises in the Middle East, NORCAP • Supports the continued efforts to safeguard protection and support to people affected by conflict and violence • Strengthens humanitarian coordination and secures access to lifesaving aid, critical protection services and infrastructure. • Enhances efforts securing the inclusion of civil society in humanitarian response planning and implementation Response focus: • Provide continued support to partners implementing responses to meet basic need of affected populations, providing emergency and inter-sector response coordination, information management, humanitarian access, logistics, shelter, WASH, cash assistance, acute food insecurity, nutrition and health needs. • Secure access to reliable and safe energy sources for people affected by displacement and infrastructure damage. • Support response mitigating the immediate exposure to protection risks and access to protection assistance. Support includes protection coordination, case management, GBV, child protection, mediation, negotiation, access coordination and civil-military coordination • The escalation in violence has led to a growing burden of trauma injuries and deteriorating mental health requiring scale up of mental health expertise and service provision. • Support the ability of national actors to engage and take lead in government emergency response coordination, civil society engagement and localisation. • During emergency and surge support secure and strengthen space, structures and procedures securing AAP approach, civil society role and inclusion in planning, coordination with government entities and UN agencies in the implementation of humanitarian responses as part of enabling transition to recovery and reconstruction. • Support education in emergencies securing displaced children safe access
